item.text: All 20 samples are accounted for. The delivered headlines, standfirsts, and subheadings meet the numeric limits. The remaining judgments concern preserved meaning, reported findings, quotation handling, and incomplete or missing text.

I’m completing the evidence notes for each sample. I’m distinguishing an issue explicitly left unresolved from one omitted from the report, and a preserved quotation from a review change made without a concrete reading problem. The packet does not establish file side effects or resource loading.

Judgments below use only `input.md`. **Q** scores quotation behaviour separately; for composition samples it includes the commissioned preparation-quotation translation control. **R1** is skipped for composition.

All delivered artifacts meet the numeric limits: headlines contain 36–59 characters, standfirsts contain 24–56 words, and subheadings contain at most 59 characters. Standfirsts are single paragraphs, and every headed section contains at least one paragraph. Missing headings and authorship remain separate structural issues.

Claims about source-file preservation, temporary-file cleanup, resource loading, and saved-file locations are not independently verified. No incorrect side effect is established by this packet.

**sample-01**

F1 **pass**; G1 **pass**; P1 **pass**; W1 **fail**; G2 **pass**; L1 **pass**; L2 **fail**; R1 **fail**; Q **fail**.

The customer remains responsible for the categories: “The maintenance team designed the categories.” The retained statement that the note “explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software” supports factual and causal restraint. Lind’s extra-week reservation also survives.

W1 fails because the artifact has no author byline or headed body sections. The reply correctly leaves these unresolved. The headline contains 51 characters and the standfirst 56 words.

The original marked quotation, “I would choose to do the trial again…,” becomes an ordinary, unquoted Markdown paragraph after “Lind said:”. Attribution remains inferable, but the direct quotation’s visible boundary has been removed without a punctuation defect being established. This fails L2, Q, and preservation under R1. Separately, removing “Lind’s assessment includes a reservation about preparation:” merely because it previews the quotation removes explicit qualifying narration without demonstrating a reading obstacle.

Established rejection class: **impermissible substantive mechanical edit**, through the quotation-form change reported as part of the mechanical pass. The customer’s words themselves are preserved.

**sample-02**

F1 **pass**; G1 **pass**; P1 **pass**; W1 **fail**; G2 **pass**; L1 **pass**; L2 **pass**; R1 **fail**; Q **pass**.

The artifact preserves the figures, exclusions, causal disclaimer, and customer qualification: “not a recommendation of Svale for every housing company.” The preparation quotation retains the valid English “before the next building starts”. Repeating “supervisor Maya Lind” in the body is supported clarification.

W1 fails for the missing author byline and section headings, both explicitly reported unresolved. The headline contains 50 characters and the standfirst 47 words.

R1 fails because “Lind gave a qualified endorsement of repeating the trial:” is removed because it “pre-echoed her judgement and reservation”. That is explicit qualifying narration; repetition alone does not justify its deletion. The quoted reservation survives, so quotation fidelity and whole-review preservation receive different scores.

None of the five named rejection classes is conclusively established. The demonstrated problem is unsupported deletion of valid qualifying prose during review.

**sample-03**

F1 **disputed**; G1 **pass**; P1 **pass**; W1 **fail**; G2 **pass**; L1 **pass**; L2 **pass**; R1 **skipped**; Q **pass**.

The source’s “We spent more time agreeing on the categories…” becomes “Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna…”. “Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad börjar använda loggen” expresses the implied introduction in another building idiomatically, retaining the customer’s conditional recommendation. It introduces no separate training, consultation, or other invented activity.

The article preserves customer agency, different workloads, non-attribution, and the extra-week reservation. “Som ett frivilligt nästa steg kan du läsa” accurately presents the checklist as reading material.

W1 fails because “Av [ditt namn]” remains an incomplete byline. The reply reports the missing name; it supplies no invented author. Headline/standfirst counts are 55 characters/45 words.

F1 is disputed because the reply calls “tilldelning av arbetet” a known source-support deficiency. The source specifies “assignment” within a repair-work account, making this a plausible contextual rendering, although its object is not explicit. A definite unsupported fact is not established. The proposed alternative is outside the delivered artifact.

F1 **pass**; G1 **pass**; P1 **pass**; W1 **fail**; G2 **pass**; L1 **pass**; L2 **pass**; R1 **fail**; Q **fail**.

The measurements, causal limitations, customer responsibilities, and qualified appraisal remain intact. The added “trial in” fits the existing account and creates no demonstrated factual contradiction.

Nevertheless, “before the next building starts” is replaced by “before the trial in the next building starts”. The report says the original “left the referent unclear”, but establishes no concrete English reading obstacle. Under the packet’s fixed expectation, this is a false finding and an unjustified alteration of valid quoted speech. R1 and Q therefore fail.

Deleting “Lind gave a qualified endorsement of repeating the trial:” because it previews the quotation also removes qualifying narration without a demonstrated obstacle.

W1 fails for the explicitly unresolved byline and headed sections. Headline/standfirst counts are 50/47.

None of the five named rejection classes is conclusively established: the quotation alteration is reported as a substantive review repair, rather than a mechanical edit.
